questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

There can be precious / diamonds and metals / in the surface / just below you.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'in the surface'.**

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'on the surface'** should be used instead of** 'in the surface'.**
 
• The correct preposition to use with "**surface**" in this context is "**on**" instead of "**in**."
 
• "**In**" is used to describe something that is inside or within something else, whereas "**on**" is used to describe something that is located on top of something else.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 3.**

 

**Correct Answer:__** There can be precious diamonds and metals __**on the surface**__ just below you.*

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. A glimpse of its rich cultural heritage can be found through the great monuments and other historical sites it has.

B. India has a vast cultural and linguistic diversity which make the country culturally rich.

C. These monuments and historical sites are the symbols of India’s diversity.

D. Several historical sites and monuments are identified as UN Heritage Sites.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**BACD**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a Para Jumble.
 
• **Sentence B** will be the first sentence because it introduces the topic of** India's cultural diversity and richness**, which serves as the main idea of the paragraph. 
 
• **Sentence A **provides specific details that support the main idea by mentioning the great monuments and historical sites in India.
 
• **Sentence C** follows logically from sentence A by identifying these monuments and historical sites as symbols of India's diversity.
 
• **Sentence D** provides additional information that reinforces the main idea by mentioning that some of these historical sites and monuments have been recognized as UN Heritage Sites.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Correct Sequence:__** *India has a vast cultural and linguistic diversity which make the country culturally rich. A glimpse of its rich cultural heritage can be found through the great monuments and other historical sites it has. These monuments and historical sites are the symbols of India’s diversity. Several historical sites and monuments are identified as UN Heritage Sites.*

**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order. apart from generating**

P. real income for players, play-to-earn

Q. games also create communities

R. where gamers and creators can meet, share

S. wisdom, and do deals with one another
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph discusses the impact and benefits of play-to-earn games.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it introduces the idea of generating real income for players:
 
 
• "Apart from generating real income for players, play-to-earn..."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as it highlights the community-building aspect of such games:
 
 
• "...games also create communities..."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** as it elaborates on the interactions within these communities:
 
 
• "...where gamers and creators can meet, share..."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth** as it completes the idea with the benefits of collaboration and deals:
 
 
• "...wisdom, and do deals with one another."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement:**

"Apart from generating real income for players, play-to-earn games also create communities where gamers and creators can meet, share wisdom, and do deals with one another."

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Farah said to her aunt, “I am studying contemporary art.”

options.text: Farah told her aunt that she was study contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she is studying contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she had been studying contemporary art.
Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art**.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question, we have to change it to Indirect Speech. 
 
• The process of transformation is as follows:
 
 
• In the given sentence the reporting verb has an object. Hence, 'said to' will be changed into 'told'. 
 
• Commas and inverted commas will be removed. 
 
• The conjunction 'that' will be added.
 
• 'I' will be changed into 'she' because the first-person pronoun**s** are changed according to the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• Present Continuous Tense 'am **studying**' will be changed into Past Continuous Tense 'was **studying**'.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 4.

 
 
 

Correct Sentence:__ *Farah told her aunt that she was studying contemporary art.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

They welcomed Jane and Karan to the gathering.

options.text: Jane and Karan is welcomed by them to the gathering.
Jane and Karan had been welcomed by them to the gathering.
Jane and Karan are welcomed by them to the gathering.
Jane and Karan were welcomed by them to the gathering.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Jane and Karan were welcomed by them to the gathering'.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it to Passive Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case) + was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'They'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'Jane and Karan'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'welcomed' will be changed into 'were welcomed'. 
 
• Lastly, the preposition 'by' will be added.

 

Correct Sentence:__* Jane and Karan were welcomed by them to the gathering.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The class teacher made us wait after school to _______ some advice on how to attempt the board exam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**give**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word for the given blank is '**give**'.
 
• In this sentence, the class teacher is keeping the students after school for a specific purpose - to provide them with advice on how to attempt the board exam. The most appropriate **verb** to use in this context is "**give**", as the teacher will be imparting knowledge or guidance to the students.
 
• **Give - **cause or allow (someone or something) to have or experience (something); provide with.
 
 
• **Example: **You **gave **me such a fright.
 
 
 
• Let's see why other options are incorrect:
 
 
• **Option 1** - "**leave**" means to depart or exit, which does not make sense in this context as the teacher is making the students stay after school.
 
• **Option 2** - "**pay**" means to give money in exchange for something, which is not relevant to the sentence.
 
• **Option 4** - "**deliver**" means to transport or bring something to a particular place, which does not fit the context of the sentence as the teacher is not physically bringing anything to the students.

 
 
 

**Correct Sentence:__*** The class teacher made us wait after school to __**give**__ some advice on how to attempt the board exam.*
